BOTH RUNS WERE IN core/utils/dnd, AND BOTH WERE ONE OBJECT WRITTEN TWICE. 53 -> 31.

  11  draggable_hook_builder_owl.js:15-25  ==  sortable_owl.js:14-24
  11  nested_sortable.js:72-84             ==  sortable.js:71-84

The first is the OWL adapter itself: the five hooks the framework-agnostic
builders are parameterised on -- addListener, setup, teardown, throttle,
wrapState -- bound to their OWL equivalents at each of the two OWL entry
points, makeDraggableHook and useSortable. Not a coincidence of formatting: a
sixth hook added to the contract would be wired at one entry point and silently
missing at the other. It is now OWL_SETUP_HOOKS, exported from
draggable_hook_builder_owl and imported by sortable_owl, and frozen --
draggable_hook_builder only ever reads off it, so the two entry points sharing
one object is safe.

The second is the head of onComputeParams in the two sortable hook builders:
the group selector read out of params.groups, the element selector narrowed to
it when there is one, and connectGroups carried across. applyGroupParams in
draggable_hook_builder_utils holds it now. What stays identical between the two
-- the destructured signature and the one call -- is 7 significant lines, under
the gate's 9-line floor, which is why the run disappears rather than shrinks.

Measured in two detached worktrees at 67ef279a0a6, one clean and one with only
these files copied in: 53 against 31. Nine dnd suites are 109 passed, and the 21
suites --affected selects for the three changed modules are 860 passed.

The three runs left are shape rather than substance, and none is deduplicable
without making the code worse: an import block two autocompletes share (12), the
tail of a Set comparison that py_compare writes with Python's == semantics and
collections/objects with JS deep-equality (10), and makeDataPoint's parameter
list beside its own call site (9).
